title: In Psalms 143 What Does This Psalm Teach Us About The Nature Of God In Times Of Trouble
paragraphs: Understanding the Nature of God in Times of Trouble: Insights from Psalm 143

Psalm 143 is a heartfelt prayer of David, written in a period of deep distress. The Psalmist turns to God with an urgent plea for mercy, guidance, and deliverance. This passage offers profound truths about God's character, especially in moments of difficulty and fear. Let’s explore what Psalm 143 teaches us about the nature of God when we face trouble.
1. God Listens to the Desperate Cry
David begins by appealing directly to God’s faithfulness and righteousness:
Hear my prayer, O Jehovah; give ear to my supplications: In thy faithfulness answer me, and in thy righteousness. - Psalm 143:1 ASV

This verse highlights God’s attentiveness. He is not distant or indifferent to our suffering. Instead, His very nature compels Him to listen to the cries of His people. The foundation for David’s request is God’s own character—His faithfulness and righteousness.
2. God is Righteous and Merciful
David confesses human unworthiness, recognizing the universal need for God’s mercy:
And enter not into judgment with thy servant; For in thy sight no man living is righteous. - Psalm 143:2 ASV

This verse reveals God’s holiness and justice—none can stand justified before Him on their own merit. Yet, by appealing to God’s mercy, David points to a God who is both just and compassionate. This tension is ultimately resolved in Christ, who provides righteousness on our behalf (Romans 3:22 ASV).
3. God is Our Refuge When Oppressed
David describes his soul as overwhelmed and crushed by the enemy. His response is not to rely on his own strength but to recall God’s past faithfulness:
I remember the days of old; I meditate on all thy doings; I muse on the work of thy hands. - Psalm 143:5 ASV
In times of trouble, God invites us to reflect on His past acts of deliverance. This remembrance strengthens our faith, reminding us that God is a proven refuge for the oppressed (Psalm 46:1 ASV).
4. God Responds to Humble Dependence
David’s posture before God is one of need and surrender:
I spread forth my hands unto thee: My soul thirsteth after thee, as a weary land. - Psalm 143:6 ASV

God is moved by our genuine dependence. He desires that we seek Him wholeheartedly, recognizing our inability to save ourselves. Jesus echoes this call to come to Him with our burdens (Matthew 11:28 ASV).
5. God Gives Guidance and Deliverance
David prays for guidance and for God’s will to be done in his life:
Cause me to hear thy lovingkindness in the morning; For in thee do I trust: Cause me to know the way wherein I should walk; For I lift up my soul unto thee. - Psalm 143:8 ASV

God is not only a deliverer but also a guide. He leads His people in paths of righteousness, especially when they are uncertain or afraid. His lovingkindness (steadfast love) is the assurance of His ongoing presence and care.
6. God Acts for the Sake of His Name
David appeals to God’s character as the basis for deliverance:
Quicken me, O Jehovah, for thy name’s sake: In thy righteousness bring my soul out of trouble. - Psalm 143:11 ASV
God’s rescue of His people is ultimately rooted in His own glory and faithfulness. Our deliverance brings honor to His name, showcasing His righteousness and mercy to the world.
Conclusion: God’s Unchanging Character in Trouble

Psalm 143 reveals a God who listens, is merciful, just, and faithful, and who responds to the humble cries of His people. In our darkest hours, we are invited to come to Him with confidence, knowing He delights to save and guide His children for the sake of His great name.
